title: Diwali Fares Are Peaking: When to Book, When to Stop Waiting
excerpt: With Diwali on November 8, last-minute fares on busy routes are already two to four times off-peak levels - flexibility on dates, airports and split tickets is now worth more than any coupon.
body:
• Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, with Dhanteras on November 6 and Bhai Dooj on November 10-11 - the return rush peaks right after Bhai Dooj, so returning on November 12-13 is usually cheaper.
  • Fares in the final two weeks before Diwali can run two to four times the off-peak price on the same route, according to EaseMyTrip booking data - waiting for a last-minute discount on peak days rarely pays.
  • Concrete check: Kanpur-Mumbai fares reported at Rs 7,475 to Rs 8,278 for November 6-9 can cross Rs 20,000 on later dates, and Kanpur-Bengaluru rises from Rs 9,177-Rs 9,446 to Rs 14,343.
  • Action steps today: search the whole week on a fare calendar, split the trip into two one-way tickets, compare nearby airports, and set a price alert instead of refreshing manually.

With Lakshmi Puja on Sunday, November 8, travellers still trying to get home for Diwali are booking into the most expensive part of the fare curve. Airlines sell seats in fare buckets, and on the Thursday to Saturday before Diwali the cheapest buckets on popular routes sold out weeks ago, according to Ease Advise. What remains is not a discount waiting to happen. It is the premium inventory airlines price for travellers whose dates cannot move.

Why waiting stops working in the final two weeks

EaseMyTrip says the six-to-eight-week window offers the best balance of fare and availability, and the final two weeks are the most expensive on most routes - two to four times the off-peak price, because demand is concentrated and pricing systems raise fares as each flight fills. Thin routes such as Delhi-Patna and Delhi-Lucknow rise steepest; high-frequency metro routes rise by less.

The Kanpur numbers show what that means in rupees. Nations Bizz reported Kanpur-Delhi at Rs 5,184 to Rs 5,499 between November 6 and 8, rising to Rs 12,114 from November 10. Kanpur-Mumbai was Rs 7,475 to Rs 8,278 during November 6-9 but can cross Rs 20,000 on some dates, and Kanpur-Bengaluru moved from Rs 9,177-Rs 9,446 to Rs 14,343 later.

What still saves money this late

Date flexibility is the largest lever left. Ease Advise recommends checking the whole week rather than a single date: flying on November 5 or 6 instead of November 7, or travelling early on Diwali morning itself, can save more than a coupon code, because most travellers want to arrive before the festival. The same logic applies at the other end. If you can work remotely for a few days or add one leave day, returning on November 12 or 13 avoids the post-Bhai Dooj peak.

Split the ticket next: on low-cost carriers a return is usually two one-way fares added together, so two one-way tickets let you take the cheapest airline each way. Then compare nearby airports - Gorakhpur, Varanasi and Lucknow for eastern Uttar Pradesh, and Dabolim (GOI) with Mopa (GOX) for Goa. Use the fare calendar on EaseMyTrip's Diwali booking guide to see the cheapest dates across a month in one view, and turn on price tracking - Google explains how to track prices on Google Flights and get an email when a tracked route changes significantly or is likely to rise.

Watch the add-ons: a low base fare can climb once baggage, seat selection and meals are added, so compare the fare-with-baggage price first. For journeys under about 600 km, consider the train - Indian Railways Tatkal opens one day before travel, at 10 AM for AC classes and 11 AM for non-AC.

The demand behind the fares

Cleartrip's PeekABoo tracker, reported on October 22 and cited by Ease Advise, showed budget hotel bookings up 201%, leisure hotel bookings up 135%, and bus bookings from Delhi up 80%. Budget rooms are selling out first, so lock a free-cancellation hotel now while you keep watching fares.

What this means for diaspora travellers

For readers in the United States flying to India and then connecting onward, the domestic leg is now the part most likely to break the budget. Book the domestic connection for November 5, 6 or the morning of November 8 where your international arrival allows it, keep the return after November 12 if you can, and set alerts on both legs today rather than waiting for a sale that peak-day demand makes unlikely.

When to stop waiting

The rule from the data is simple. If your dates are fixed to the peak days, book the best fare you can find now - each refresh is more likely to be higher, not lower. If you have even one day of flexibility, spend an hour on the calendar view, split tickets and nearby airports first. That hour, not a last-minute discount, is where the remaining savings are.
